title: Let a CI plug-in unsubscribe itself in the middle of a build event

blocks.text: The CI server tells its plug-ins about every finished build through `BuildEvents`. The release-notes plug-in only wants the first green build after a release branch is cut, so it unsubscribes itself from inside its callback. Since it shipped, two things happened: on the day it was installed first, the build event failed and no plug-in after it heard that build; on a server where it was installed second, the dashboard silently lost one build.

`subscribe`, `unsubscribe` and `listenerCount` work. Finish `publish(String buildId)` in `src/main/java/practice/BuildEvents.java` so that every plug-in subscribed when the event starts hears it, wherever a plug-in that leaves sits in the list, and `publish` never fails because of it. About three lines in total.

cases.says: with no plug-in leaving, every subscribed plug-in hears every build, in subscription order
a plug-in at the head of the list that unsubscribes itself makes nothing throw, the others still hear that build, and it hears no later one
the plug-in right after one that unsubscribes itself still hears the same build

origin.section: A Listener That Unsubscribes During a Dispatch Changes the List Being Walked

concepts: Dispatching over a CopyOnWriteArrayList or a copy taken first makes leaving safe: the leaver still gets the current event and no later one, and every other listener gets it.

A listener that removes itself while a for-each walks an ArrayList of listeners makes the dispatch throw ConcurrentModificationException or silently skip the listener after it, depending on where it sits.
